purpose: Enumerate immutable release artifacts that may serve as a rollback target, with the verification evidence that qualifies each one. A rollback target is selected from this registry, never from a moving ref.

target_contract.must_be_immutable: A pinned provider artifact id (e.g. a Vercel deployment id). Never a branch, tag, or 'current main', all of which move and can carry work that was merged but never released.
target_contract.must_have_exact_source: The exact source commit the artifact was built from.
target_contract.must_have_capability_manifest: The routes and capabilities the artifact is known to serve, so a rollback cannot silently drop functionality.
target_contract.must_have_verification: Either production_verified (it served production and was verified there) or rehearsal_verified (deployed to non-production and probed). Anything else is a candidate, not a target.
target_contract.selection_rule: At incident start, select the most recent artifact with qualified=true whose capability manifest covers the required routes, and pin its exact id. Re-read the artifact from the provider before promoting it. If no qualified target exists, rollback is UNAVAILABLE and forward recovery is the safe path.
target_contract.identifier_validation: Artifact identifiers are validated against a per-provider ALLOWLIST of immutable id shapes (vercel: dpl_ plus a long base62 token). An earlier version blocklisted origin/*, refs/*, main and HEAD, which let v1.2.3, release/foo and feature/x qualify. A provider with no registered id shape cannot contribute a target.

artifacts.capability_manifest_source: prior production verification recorded in Pandora Memory and ops/projectos-memory-connector-recovery-2026-08-10.md; health and Memory search were probed end-to-end after deployment
artifacts.qualification_note: Qualified as the rollback target for any FUTURE deployment: it is immutable, production-verified, and carries the full current capability set. It is not a rollback target for itself — it is what production is running now.
limitations: The capability manifest was not re-probed in this pass; Vercel is unauthenticated in this session.
The source commit is asserted by prior evidence and was not independently rebound to the artifact.

artifacts.capability_manifest_source: predates the restoration of the ProjectOS health and Memory search routes
artifacts.qualification_note: DISQUALIFIED as a capability-preserving rollback target. Promoting it would restore a working Memory while silently dropping /api/projectos/health and /api/projectos/memory/search — a partial outage presented as a recovery.

explicitly_not_targets.reason: A moving ref. Current main can contain work that was merged but never production-authorized, deployed, rehearsed, or production-verified. Promoting it during an incident would ship unreleased changes instead of restoring known-good state. An earlier revision of the rollback procedure made exactly this mistake.
Mutable. A tag can be moved and a branch advances; neither is a pinned artifact.

current_status.rehearsal_gate: No rehearsal has been performed. Availability here means a qualified artifact exists and is selectable, NOT that promoting it has been exercised end to end.
current_status.coverage_note: This registry covers the Vercel web tier only. Edge Functions version independently at Supabase and do not roll back with a web promotion. No applied migration has rollback metadata, so there is no database rollback path at all. A change spanning the web tier and the database is not rollback-safe.
